summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for recurrent nausea and vomiting that began after taking morning medications on an empty stomach. She had no abdominal pain or signs of infection, and labs showed no metabolic derangement. Her symptoms improved with bowel rest, IV fluids, and symptom management. The hospital course was complicated by hypoglycemia due to reduced oral intake, prompting a temporary reduction in her evening Lantus insulin from 28 to 24 units. She gradually advanced to a regular diet, remained nausea-free, and was discharged home with instructions to resume her normal insulin dose when eating normally and to follow up with her primary care provider.
